lessonRef.title: Investigation or close reading: principal annual percentage rate and term
lessonRef.focus: principal annual percentage rate and term

objective: Learners annualise an invented short-term borrowing fee and compare it with a conventional annual rate.
scenario: Kwabena is an invented eighth grader investigating a pretend short-term loan: $1,200.00 borrowed with a $180.00 fee for a four-week term, renewable. A simulated year holds 13 such terms. A conventional invented alternative charges 30% a year.
safetyNotes: Every amount, person, business, and account in this task is invented for practice. Nothing here refers to a real household.
Never write a real bank account, card, PIN, password, Social Security, or tax number on this sheet; the task never asks for one.
This is education, not individualized financial advice. Real money decisions belong to a trusted adult.

tasks.directions: The lender describes the charge as 15% of the amount borrowed for each four-week term. Check that this rate matches the $180.00 fee actually quoted on Kwabena's invented loan.

prompts.text: What does 15% of the $1,200.00 borrowed come to?

tasks.directions: Project the fee across all 13 invented terms in a simulated year, then compute the conventional alternative at 30%.

prompts.text: What do 13 terms of the fee come to in a year?
What would 30% a year cost on the same $1,200.00?

tasks.directions: Compare the two annual costs for Kwabena and express the short-term arrangement against the amount borrowed.

prompts.text: How much more does the short-term arrangement cost in a year?
By how much do a year of fees exceed the amount originally borrowed?

tasks.directions: The advertised figure was a flat fee, not a rate.

prompts.text: Explain why quoting a flat fee for a short term hides the cost, and describe how Kwabena converted it into something comparable.

remediation: If a learner treats one term as a year, mark how many terms fit in a simulated year for Kwabena before any annual figure is computed.
extension: Ask the learner what flat fee per term would make Kwabena's short-term loan match the 30% annual alternative.

items.promptText: What does 15% of the $1,200.00 borrowed come to?
What do 13 terms of the fee come to in a year?
What would 30% a year cost on the same $1,200.00?

By how much do a year of fees exceed the amount originally borrowed?
